item.title: LAERZ — Thu Oct 1, 7:00 PM — Songbyrd
item.description: LAERZ is an LA based electronic artist redefining what a DJ set can be. Blurring the line between live production and performance, he builds tracks in real time, stacking cinematic vocals, sculpting synths, triggering drum pads, and weaving loops into fully immersive, high voltage moments. No two sets are the same. Every drop is built live. Every chorus feels earned. He first captured global attention through his busking style performances and on the spot content creation, transforming sidewalks and unexpected spaces into stages. That raw, human approach resonated, building a fiercely organic audience of over 4 million followers across social media. That momentum translated offline as well, culminating in a 22 date headline tour that brought his immersive live show to audiences across the country. What began as viral moments has evolved into something more focused: intentional releases crafted to live far beyond the scroll. Sonically, LAERZ exists where emotional depth meets dancefloor

item.title: The R&B Club Discusses The Legacy of Aaliyah — Sun Aug 23, 12:00 PM — Songbyrd
item.description: Certain moments in this century have stayed with us. And they always will. August 25, 2001, is just that. It seems almost surreal to say, but The R&B Club’s next event comes almost a quarter-century to the day that the R&B icon Aaliyah tragically passed away. There's no way not to have a connection to her music, but more importantly, Aaliyah herself. If you know anything about us, and what we pride ourselves on, this won't be simply music being played. This is a voyage and a trip back in time into one of the most captivating and abbreviated careers in music history. We’ll discuss it all. The highs, the classic records, where we were when we got the news of her death — and, yes, the R. Kelly of it all. It's one time for Babygirl (better known as Aaliyah) on Sunday, August 23, at the only home we've ever known in Songbyrd. Tickets are $15 in advance and $20 at the door — pending there's any left. item.description: Thursday September 10th ZACK KEIM x GARDENER w/ THE DUSKWHALES, STEPHEN SOL \*\*\* ZACK KEIM His second solo album, titled “Battery Lane” is out now via Evan Westfall of Caamp’s indie label Super Sport Records. Named after the street where Keim lived during his time in the DC area, the album reflects the people and places that inspired this chapter of his songwriting. From 2025 to 2026, he toured extensively throughout the US/Europe/and UK. Keim's powerful live performances have led him to play SXSW and share the stage with renowned artists such as Peter Case (The Nerves/Plimsouls), indie icon Calvin Johnson (Beat Happening/founder of K Records), and acclaimed singer-songwriter Matt Costa. His standout single, “Better Days,” has received praise from Sirius XMU calling it “a fun, fuzzy, classic.” GARDENER Hailing from Yellow Springs, OH, Gardener is a close-knit group of old friends. Formed in 2021 in the basement of their house in Charlottesville, Virginia, Spoonfed has grown from late-night jam sessions into one of the DMV's emerging indie bands. Spoonfed draws inspiration from the grunge rock of the 1990s, the alt-rock of the early 2000s, and the grooves of modern funk. Expect energy: dark and uplifting melodies, dynamic rhythms, moody lyrics, guitar solos. Blige, and dozens more. She co wrote the Billy Ray Cyrus verse that turned "Old Town Road" into the fastest Diamond certified song in RIAA history. She gave Beyoncé "Virgo's Groove." She penned Summer Walker's "Body" and SZA's "Low." She scored Spider Man: Across the Spider Verse. Raised in the lineage of Memphis soul royalty, her mother sang alongside Al Green and Ann Peebles at Hi Records. Jozzy honed her craft under the mentorship of Timbaland and Missy Elliott before becoming one of the most commercially impactful writers of her generation. item.title: Guerilla Toss — Tue Oct 20, 7:00 PM — Songbyrd
item.description: When NYC-based experimental dance punks Guerilla Toss, active since time immemorial aka 2011, were in Vermont recording their new full-length album You’re Weird Now, frontwoman Kassie Carlson would prepare what she called ‘punk lunch’: a communal meal made by raiding the studio fridge for whatever was left and assembling a sandwich from the most random ingredients imaginable. Regularly joining punk lunch were two legends from their own corners of the weird music world: Stephen Malkmus (Pavement, The Jicks) and Trey Anastasio, Phish guitarist and owner of The Barn; the recording studio where Guerilla Toss were making You’re Weird Now, with Malkmus in the producer’s seat. Engineer Bryce Goggin, who has worked with Malkmus since Crooked Rain, Crooked Rain, and Ben Collette, Phish’s longtime engineer at The Barn, were also part of the crew. item.description: Sunday October 25th Renny Conti w/ James Eichman \*\*\* Through his early twenties, Renny self-released a string of homemade albums, sorting out his aesthetic and narrative viewpoint as a musician before his project began in earnest. His self-titled debut was recorded in 2023, collecting older material that served as a proper introduction to him as an artist. Finally released in 2025, the album soon earned him buzz across the indie landscape, and landed him a deal with Mom+Pop. Once more, Split Second feels like a long-awaited debut: Emerging from not only 2023 but all the years before, Split Second catalogues the snapshots and places and people that made Renny the musician he is today. Renny’s life in music began as it does for many of us: a means of escape from the confusing pivot from childhood to teenage years.
